history.origins: Alexander Tvaladze describes a Russian version of the commerce game known as три палки (Three Sticks), a variant of the Schwimmen (31) family. The 31/commerce group is popular in Germany, Austria, and Russia; this Russian variant uses a 36-card pack and stick penalties for the lowest hand.
timeline: Traditional: Russian folk game; played informally in Russia.

setup.deck: 36 cards (6-A). Values: A=11, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 10=-10, 9=0, 6-8=Face value.

rules.objective: Collect cards of one suit totalling 31 points or a special hand; avoid having the lowest score to avoid receiving sticks; three sticks mean elimination; last player left wins.
rules.gameplay: 1. Play a card to the center. 2. Add its value to running total. 3. Draw a replacement card. 4. If total > 31, earn a 'palka' (stick). Total resets. 5. Three sticks = out.

strategy.basic: Play small cards when total is high. Save 10s to 'reduce' the total.
strategy.intermediate: Play 10s and 9s strategically to control when the total is near 31.
strategy.advanced: Calculate what opponents are likely holding. Force them to bust.

scoring.description: Palki (sticks) are penalty points. 3 = elimination. Last player standing wins.
